title: The Centipede in Its Skin
text:
The centipede sheds in the longest dark of the year of its life that it is willing to acknowledge.

A centipede that sheds early is a centipede that has miscounted. A centipede that sheds late is a centipede that is hoping. The basin centipede sheds, in the keeping of an honest keeper, on the night the basin's water reaches the precise temperature at which the keeper, lying on the floor beside it, would also wish to be unbecoming for an hour.

The shed reads as follows. Count the segments — fewer than the body's age means a segment was left in the previous year's molt; more means the keeper has lost a season somewhere. The seventh segment is the segment of temper; pale, the centipede will be slow to milk this year and will not bite a clean hand. The twenty-third is the segment of the dantian-mirror; pale, the venom this year will be honest — the milking-cup may be of bronze, not gold. The antennae read time itself; if they curl tight to the body's centre, the centipede shed in fear, and the keeper has six days to learn what the basin saw before the basin saw it.

Apothecary Qi reads the husk under the second lamp from the left, which is the lamp that does not flicker. She does not write the reading down. She writes everything else down. The reading is the one thing the keeper carries in the body, where the basin-creatures keep their counts as well.

title: The Spider Who Remembers Silk
text:
The basin spider stops spinning for two reasons and only two.

The first is dying. The spinneret slows; the silk thins; the body begins the slow work of withdrawing from the body. The fifth basin's spider, in this case, will not refuse food but will not pursue it; the keeper will set the wax-moth on the rim of the bronze and the spider will accept it without rising, and the keeper will know.

The second is the egg-sac. The spider gathers her silk inwards for the sac she has not yet shown the keeper, and she will not show the keeper for thirteen nights, and on the fourteenth she will be lighter by the weight of three hundred small white things she will then guard with the patience of a sentry whose tour does not end.

The difficulty is that both look identical for the first nine days.

The book that distinguishes them — the *Treatise on the Two Silences* by Lan-yi's third disciple, whose name has been kept off the spine — is in the Matriarch's library. Apothecary Qi has not read it. Bai of the Garden has read it, in a copy she keeps under the iron lattice; she does not say where she keeps it, and the Garden does not say where she keeps it, and the keeper of the basin does not ask. The keeper does not need the book. She needs the answer.

The Garden's answer, this season, was the egg-sac. Apothecary Qi inclined her head once when she heard, and brought a smaller wax-moth to the basin, and did not lift the ladle for two weeks.

title: The Scorpion's First Bite
text:
A basin-born scorpion is not the same animal as one taken from the gorge. The basin's water is in her from the first hour; the basin's count is in her from the third. She knows the keeper before she knows her own legs. Her first bite is the basin's first bite — not the gorge's, not the world's — and the bite must be received into a cup the basin will recognise, sealed with a wrapping the basin has felt before, set into the sect's count by a hand the basin has learned to permit.

The rite is at moonless midnight, and three pairs of hands are needed. The mother's hand is the keeper's. The daughter's hand is the keeper's also, but the keeper cannot hold both at once; a second pair is the apothecary's apprentice — or, when the basin is between apprentices, the gardener of the iron lattice. The third pair the daughter chooses on the night, by stepping toward one of the hands offered. Such a hand, the keepers say, does not refuse. The basin hears the refusal even when the lamp does not.

Apothecary Qi has performed this rite four times in her keepership. Twice the third hand was the gardener's. Once it was a junior of the gorge who came on the right night by accident. Once — long before the present Matriarch — the third hand was a stranger from the Crossing whose face the basin remembered the next year, and the year after, and the year after that. The basin's memory is the long memory of the sect, which is to say, the memory the sect would not pretend to have.

The sealed cup is set into the count for a year. At the next moonless midnight of the next year the cup is opened, and the sister-mother is asked, by sound only — three small bronze chimes from a third-hand position the keeper does not occupy — whether the daughter has lived. The basin answers. The keeper writes it down. The cup is rinsed in basin-water and set away.

title: The Keeper's Silence
text:
Apothecary Qi was not born to the rolls. Her name is in the dispensary book and in the count of the basins, and she does not appear in the sect's other records — the founding ledger, the line of inheritances, the list of those whose hand may take the hundred-grass at midnight. She is the keeper, which is not a daughter. The Matriarch is the daughter the basins keep above the keeper.

This is not a wound. Qi has been asked, twice in her keepership, whether she would consent to be entered into the rolls — once by the previous Matriarch, who liked her, and once by the present Matriarch, who likes her better. Twice she has declined.

'A keeper,' she said the second time, 'has hands the rolls would not be honest about. The rolls are a thing the sect believes. The basins are a thing the basins believe. I am better in the second book.'

The present Matriarch did not press the matter. She did, that evening, set a small grey silk knot at the apothecary's wrist — the same knot Lan-yi's first apprentice had worn, kept in a drawer for a hundred years — and Qi has not taken it off since.

The sect speaks of two ways of belonging: the rolls and the keeping. The rolls are honest about a great deal and quiet about a small remainder. The keeping is the quiet itself, made into a wrist-knot and set down beside a bronze basin at the second-best lamp.
